entry: French professional wrestler and actor. Dubbed the "Eighth Wonder of the World," he was known for his great size, which resulted from gigantism caused by excess human growth hormone. He relocated to North America in 1971 and became a mainstay of the World Wrestling Federation in the 1980s. In 1988 he defeated [[Hulk Hogan]] to win the WWF World Heavyweight Championship. Outside wrestling he is best known for playing Fezzik in *The Princess Bride* (1987).

American tennis player. He won eight major singles titles, 60 ATP Tour singles titles and an Olympic gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. He returned to the world No. 1 ranking in 1999 after completing the career Golden Slam at the French Open. He retired after the 2006 U.S. Open. He has been married to [[Steffi Graf]] since 2001.

Italian tenor. He rose to fame in 1994 after winning the newcomers' section of the 44th Sanremo Music Festival. He has recorded 15 solo studio albums and nine complete operas since 1994, selling over 90 million records worldwide. His album *Romanza* is one of the best-selling albums of all time. He has been visually impaired since birth because of congenital glaucoma.

Italian Renaissance architect active in the Venetian Republic. Influenced by Roman and Greek architecture, above all the writings of [[Vitruvius]], he designed churches and palaces but was best known for country houses and villas. His treatise *The Four Books of Architecture* (Venice, 1570) gained him wide recognition and influenced later architects, including [[Thomas Jefferson]]. Trained as a stonemason in Vicenza, he was employed in 1538–1539 by the humanist Gian Giorgio Trissino, who introduced him to the monuments of ancient Rome and gave him the name Palladio. The city of Vicenza, with 23 buildings designed by Palladio, and his 24 villas in the [[Veneto]] are listed by [[UNESCO]] as a [[World Heritage Site]].

Flemish anatomist and physician, often regarded as the founder of modern human [[Anatomy|anatomy]]. He taught surgery and anatomy at the University of Padua from 1537 to 1542 and later served as imperial physician at the court of Emperor Charles V. His *Tabulae anatomicae sex* (1538) consisted of six large woodcut posters that were widely copied. His *De humani corporis fabrica libri septem*, published in [[Basel]] in 1543, was based on direct observation and identified over 200 anatomical inaccuracies in the work of [[Galen]], whose texts had long dominated anatomy. Vesalius made [[Dissection|dissection]] the central method of teaching, performing it himself before students.

Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist. He worked in the Soviet nuclear weapons program and played a key role in developing the first megaton-range Soviet hydrogen bomb. He also did fundamental work in [[Particle physics|particle physics]], magnetism and [[Physical cosmology|physical cosmology]]. From the late 1960s he campaigned for human rights and civil liberties, and Soviet authorities deemed him a dissident and subjected him to persecution. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1975. After internal exile in Gorky from 1980, he was released in 1986. The European Parliament awards the annual Sakharov Prize in his memory.

Soviet film director and screenwriter of Russian origin. His films are known for slow pacing, long takes, dreamlike imagery and a preoccupation with nature and memory. He directed his first five features in the [[Soviet Union]], beginning with *Ivan's Childhood* (1962), which won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival. Later films included *Andrei Rublev* (1966), *Solaris* (1972), *Mirror* (1975) and *Stalker* (1979). After conflicts with state film authorities he left the country in 1979 and made his last two features abroad, *Nostalghia* (1983) and *The Sacrifice* (1986). Three of his films were included in *Sight & Sound*'s 2012 poll of the 100 greatest films of all time.

Scottish-born American industrialist and philanthropist. He emigrated with his family from Dunfermline to [[Pittsburgh]] in 1848, at age 12, and later invested in railroads, bridges and oil. He built the Carnegie Steel Company, which he sold to [[J. P. Morgan]] in 1901 for $303,450,000; the company formed the basis of the U.S. Steel Corporation. His essay "The Gospel of Wealth" (1889) argued that the rich should use their fortunes for public benefit. He gave away around $350 million, almost 90 percent of his fortune, to libraries, universities and peace efforts, including Carnegie Hall and the Peace Palace in [[The Hague]]. The 1892 Homestead Strike at his Pennsylvania mill ended in a lockout and an armed clash with Pinkerton agents, with several deaths; Carnegie was in Scotland at the time.

American general and seventh president of the United States (1829–1837). He became a national hero after his victory at the Battle of [[New Orleans]] in 1815, and he led U.S. forces in the First Seminole War, a campaign that helped prompt Spain to cede [[Florida]]. As a wealthy planter at The Hermitage he profited from the forced labor of hundreds of enslaved African Americans. His supporters formed the coalition that became the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]]. In 1830 he signed the Indian Removal Act, which displaced tens of thousands of Native Americans and led to thousands of deaths on the [[Trail of Tears]]; the act has been described as ethnic cleansing. In 1835 he became the only U.S. president to pay off the national debt. Supporters credit him with defending democracy and the Constitution. Critics point to his policies toward Native Americans and his willingness to ignore the law.

American politician and 17th president of the United States (1865–1869). He succeeded to the presidency after the assassination of [[Abraham Lincoln]] and favored quick restoration of the seceded states, with few protections for formerly enslaved people. Congress repeatedly overrode his vetoes of Reconstruction legislation. The House impeached him in 1868, and the Senate acquitted him by one vote. In 1875 he was elected to the Senate, the only former president to serve in that body. Historians have generally ranked him among the worst U.S. presidents.

English composer and impresario of musical theatre. He has composed 21 musicals, including *Jesus Christ Superstar*, *Evita*, *Cats* and *The Phantom of the Opera*, several of which have run for more than a decade in the [[West End theatre|West End]] and on Broadway. Songs such as "Memory" and "The Music of the Night" have been widely recorded outside their shows. In 2001 *The New York Times* called him "the most commercially successful composer in history." He was knighted in 1992 and later made a life peer. He has won seven Tony Awards and an Academy Award, and in 2018 he became the thirteenth person to win an Oscar, an Emmy, a Grammy and a Tony. His company, LW Entertainment, is one of the largest theatre operators in London.

Soviet mathematician associated with the creation of modern [[Probability theory|probability theory]]. In 1933 he gave probability a rigorous axiomatic foundation based on measure theory. He graduated from Moscow State University in 1925 and earned his Doctor of Philosophy degree there in 1929.In 1922 he constructed a [[Fourier series|Fourier series]] that diverges almost everywhere, which brought him international recognition. He also contributed to [[Topology|topology]], intuitionistic logic, [[Turbulence|turbulence]], [[Classical mechanics|classical mechanics]] and [[Functional analysis|functional analysis]]. In the 1960s he co-initiated algorithmic information theory, defining the complexity of a string as the length of the shortest program that describes it.

King of Imerina on [[Madagascar]] (r. 1787–1810). He reunited Imerina after 77 years of civil war and then extended his kingdom over the Betsileo, Sihanaka, Bezanozano and Bara territories, with the aim of uniting Madagascar under Merina rule. He established his capital at the fortified town of Ambohimanga, which [[UNESCO]] designated a World Heritage Site in 2001. The Merina regard him as a cultural hero, and he is considered one of the greatest military and political leaders in the history of Madagascar. His son Radama I continued his conquests.

Ukrainian football player and manager. He began his career at [[Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]], winning five league titles in a row. He scored 48 goals for the Ukraine national team, its all-time top scorer, and captained the team to the quarter-finals of the 2006 [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]]. While at [[AC Milan]] and Chelsea he reached three [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] finals, winning the 2003 final, and with Milan he won [[Serie A]] in 2004. He received the Ballon d'Or in 2004. In January 2024 he was elected president of the Ukrainian Football Association.

Operating system for mobile devices, developed by Google. Based on a modified version of the [[Linux]] kernel and other [[Open-source software|open-source software]], it was first released in 2008. Android is the most used operating system for [[Smartphone|smartphones]] and has over three billion monthly active users. Its developer, Android Inc., was founded in Palo Alto, California, in 2003 and acquired by Google in 2005. Most devices ship with proprietary Google software, including Google Mobile Services, which bundles [[Google Chrome]] and the Google Play store. Android has also been adapted for televisions, wearables, cars and virtual reality headsets.

Humanoid robot or other artificial being, often made from a flesh-like material. Androids were long confined to [[Science fiction|science fiction]], but advances in robotics have produced machines with human-like forms. Karel Čapek's play *R.U.R.* (1921), which introduced the word [[Robot|robot]], featured organic artificial humans. The term *droid* derives from an abridgment of "android" and was popularized by [[George Lucas]] in *Star Wars*.

Barred spiral galaxy and the nearest major galaxy to the [[Milky Way]]. Also known as Messier 31 (M31), it lies about 765 kpc (2.5 million light-years) from Earth in the constellation Andromeda. Its D25 isophotal diameter is about 46.56 kpc (152,000 light-years), making it the largest member of the [[Local Group]]. In c. 964 the Persian astronomer Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi described it as a "nebulous smear." [[Edwin Hubble|Edwin Hubble]] confirmed in 1925 that it lies beyond the Milky Way. It is estimated to contain about one trillion stars and is visible to the naked eye under dark skies.

Postulated galactic collision between the [[Milky Way]] and the [[Andromeda Galaxy]]. The Andromeda Galaxy is approaching the Milky Way at about 110 km/s, and earlier estimates predicted a merger in about 4.5 billion years. A 2025 study using data from the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] and the Gaia spacecraft put the chance of a head-on collision within the next 10 billion years at 50 percent. Stars are so widely spaced that direct stellar collisions would be improbable.

American actor, comedian and singer. He is best known for playing Sheriff Andy Taylor in the [[CBS]] sitcom *The Andy Griffith Show* (1960–1968), set in the fictional town of Mayberry, [[North Carolina]]. He later starred as the defense attorney Ben Matlock in the [[NBC]] drama *Matlock* (1986–1995). He made his film debut in *A Face in the Crowd* (1957), directed by [[Elia Kazan]]. He received two Tony Award nominations for Broadway performances.

American entertainer and performance artist. He disdained conventional jokes and was sometimes called an "anti-comedian." He first appeared on [[Saturday Night Live]] in 1975. His role as Latka Gravas on the sitcom *Taxi* (1978–1983) brought him wider fame. In 1982 he brought a staged wrestling feud with Jerry Lawler to *Late Night with David Letterman*; the planned nature of the encounter was not disclosed for over a decade.

American artist and filmmaker. Born in [[Pittsburgh]] to Rusyn immigrant parents, he was a leading figure of the [[Pop art|pop art]] movement, whose work explored advertising, consumerism, mass media and celebrity. His silkscreen paintings include *Campbell's Soup Can* (1961–62) and *Marilyn Diptych* (1962). In the mid-1960s he made experimental films such as *Empire* (1965) and *Chelsea Girls* (1966) at the Factory, his New York studio. He managed [[The Velvet Underground]] and survived an assassination attempt in 1968. Afterward the Factory became a business enterprise, and he founded *Interview* magazine. *Shot Sage Blue Marilyn* sold for $195 million in 2022, the highest price paid at auction for a work by an American artist.

Blood disorder in which the blood has a reduced ability to carry oxygen. The cause may be a lower-than-normal number of [[Red blood cell|red blood cells]], a reduced amount of [[Hemoglobin|hemoglobin]], or abnormal hemoglobin that impairs its function. Symptoms can include tiredness, weakness, shortness of breath and reduced ability to exercise. Anemia can result from blood loss, decreased red blood cell production or increased red blood cell breakdown; causes include iron deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, [[Malaria]] and sickle cell anemia. Severe anemia can lead to [[Heart failure]]. Diagnosis in men is based on hemoglobin below 130 g/L, and in non-pregnant women below 120 g/L.

Bulge or balloon-like swelling in the wall of a blood vessel, caused by a localized weakness. Aneurysms may be hereditary or acquired, and they often develop without symptoms. As an aneurysm grows, the risk of rupture rises, which can cause uncontrolled bleeding. Most affect arteries. The most dangerous include cerebral aneurysms in the [[Brain|brain]] and aortic aneurysms in the chest and abdomen. Risk factors include [[Blood pressure|high blood pressure]], smoking and [[Atherosclerosis]]. Aneurysms occur in about 1–2 percent of the population. Aneurysms can also serve as the starting point for blood clots, and they can arise in the heart after a [[Myocardial infarction|heart attack]].

Taiwanese filmmaker. His films are known for emotional restraint and for exploring repressed and hidden emotions. He first gained fame in Taiwan with the *Father Knows Best* trilogy: *Pushing Hands*, *The Wedding Banquet* and *Eat Drink Man Woman*. His Hollywood breakthrough was *Sense and Sensibility* (1995), an adaptation of [[Jane Austen]], followed by *Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon* (2000), *Brokeback Mountain* (2005) and *Life of Pi* (2012). He has won two [[Academy Awards|Academy Awards]] and three Golden Globe Awards, and he is the only filmmaker to have won the Golden Bear twice.

Waterfall in [[Venezuela]], the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall. Its total height is 979 m (3,212 ft), including a main plunge of 807 m (2,648 ft). It drops from the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in Canaima National Park, a [[World Heritage Site]] in the Gran Sabana region of Bolívar State. Its water flows into the Churún River, a tributary of the [[Orinoco]]. The falls were named after the American aviator James Angel, who first saw them from the air in 1937. Whether they are taller than South Africa's Tugela Falls remains uncertain, because the measurements were taken at a considerable distance.
